detaileddescription.para: Every point is drawn as a GPU billboard with one of the marker shapes shared with LineCurve. Points are colored uniformly with color, or by a per-point scalar value mapped through colormap. Points are colored uniformly while colormap is null or no values are stored.

Positions and values are uploaded as a single data texture; the vertex buffer depends only on the point count, so updating a cloud of constant size is one texture upload per frame. Methods whose names end in F take interleaved float XY pairs [x0, y0, x1, y1, …] and an optional value vector with one float per point. postData() may be called from any thread.

simplesect.title: Invalid points
simplesect.para: Non-finite coordinates, and non-positive coordinates on a logarithmic axis, are kept in storage so indices stay stable, but they are not drawn, not hit-tested, and do not contribute to data ranges. A point with a non-finite value is drawn with the uniform color.

simplesect.title: Transitions
simplesect.para: Assign a MorphTransition or DrawTransition to transition to animate data updates. With MorphTransition, points move to their new position, and their values, when the old and the new points both have them, change with them. New points appear, and removed points disappear, at once. count, pointAt(), valueAt(), the data and value ranges, and inspection use the new data from the start of the animation, while hover picks the points as drawn. While a transition is enabled, setValues() animates as well and the setDataF() overloads store doubles. clearData(), and replacing, clearing, or cancelling transition, skip to the new data.

simplesect.title: Limits
simplesect.para: Coordinates are single precision. The number of renderable points is bounded by the GPU's maximum texture size: about 22 million points with values, or 33 million without, for an 8192-pixel limit, and twice that for 16384. Points beyond it are not drawn or hovered, and a warning is logged once.
